description: TikTok delivery through the Content Posting API. This is the richest machine-readable specification TikTok publishes and the only one enumerating codecs, frame-rate bounds and pixel minimums and maximums.
caveats: TikTok's own documentation gives four different official maximum durations across overlapping upload paths: 10 minutes for this API, 30 minutes for TikTok Studio, and 60 minutes for in-app upload (10 minutes for in-app recording). Pick the preset that matches how you will actually deliver.
TikTok re-encodes every upload, so many properties are silently normalised rather than rejected. Only the published API restriction table is enforced here.

TikTok publishes nothing about codec profile/level, HDR, colour, bit depth, chroma subsampling, fast start, pixel aspect ratio, GOP, interlacing, or loudness. Those are reported as unknown, never judged.

sources.title: Media Transfer Guide — Video restrictions, TikTok for Developers
Get Started — Direct Post / Upload, TikTok for Developers
Tools for creators (TikTok Studio), TikTok Help Center

rules.explanation: Supported media formats are MP4 (recommended), WebM and MOV.
Supported codecs are H.264 (recommended), H.265, VP8 and VP9.
Width must be at least 360 and at most 4096 pixels.
Height must be at least 360 and at most 4096 pixels.
Frame rate must be a minimum of 23 and a maximum of 60 FPS.
The longest video that can be sent through the upload endpoint is 10 minutes.
rules.note: Other TikTok delivery paths document different maximums; see this preset's caveats.

rules.explanation: AAC audio is recommended (the documented example pairs H.264 with AAC).
rules.message_fail: TikTok does not state a hard audio codec rule and re-encodes every upload.

rules.explanation: 9:16 is the native and recommended aspect ratio.
rules.message_fail: 1:1 and 16:9 are also accepted and are letterboxed on playback.
720x1280 is the documented minimum for the Studio upload path; this is a quality recommendation only.

rules.explanation: A constant frame rate avoids reinterpretation during TikTok's server-side transcode.
rules.message_fail: TikTok publishes no VFR policy; this is quality guidance only.

rules.explanation: TikTok Studio web upload documents a 30-minute maximum.
rules.note: Reported so the contradiction between TikTok's own published limits is visible rather than silently resolved.

rules.explanation: In-app upload documents a 60-minute maximum (10 minutes for in-app recording).
rules.note: Reported so the contradiction between TikTok's own published limits is visible rather than silently resolved.

rules.explanation: Colour transfer characteristics, reported for information.
rules.note: TikTok publishes no HDR, colour, bit-depth or chroma acceptance criteria.
